title: Deleted all of my recipes
body: I got a new phone and my data didn’t sync automatically. When I signed in on the old phone, it deleted every recipe that I wrote.

title: double charged
body: paid lifetime subscription and was unable to cancel. tech support does not seem to exist. discord link does not work. am being charged monthly as well as having paid fifty bucks. opened dispute with apple due to lack of options.

title: Really?
body: After years of support you decide to do a Premium as a screw you to people who were loyal to you very early in your app… I’m done you’re greedy. You should grandfather in people who supported you.

title: Lost everything
body: Premium subscriber with a Mixel account. Got a new phone, opened Mixel and signed into my Mixel account to find that I’ve lost all of my recipes, bookmarks, favorites, inventory, etc. I am NOT pleased.

title: Keyboard Covers Links
body: I have been a paid subscriber to this wonderful app for a while, but the most recent update has a glitch that needs to be addressed. The keyboard rises up to cover parts of the screen that you need to click on in order to follow links and make the recipes. There does not seem to be a way to get rid of it. Please fix this! Thank you. I literally can’t access some of the information because the keyboard covers it.

title: Dishonest
body: Lists a one time payment option of $29 for premium. When you get into the app, however, they only give you the option for ongoing subscriptions. If you’re going to gouge people with subscriptions, at least be honest about it in the app description instead of tricking them into downloading the app.

title: Too hard to figure out
body: I want an app where you can put what ingredients you have and it will come up with drink recipes. Tho this app claims to do it... I couldn’t figure out how. If I ask my 14 yr old grandson to help me create my profile, would it be illegal cause he’s not 21? Hahaha I am gonna keep searching.

title: Very confusing
body: Couldn’t even figure out to follow the tutorial. Useless app.

title: UX completely non-intuitive
body: I tried for five minutes to figure out how to add ingredients to my bar, but I could only trash them, open information about them, and add them to my shopping list. And I couldn’t find the shopping list. It’s a great idea, but it’s impossible to use.

title: Nope - don’t waste yer time
body: Cool, does not work.

title: Great idea...
body: ...however, the pixel aesthetic makes it incredibly hard to read or understand anything on the screen. It’s impossible to use with one hand as all of the actions are up top. Shame really as I would love to use the app if the design wasn’t so bad.

title: Hurts the eyes
body: Sorry but the graphics in this app are so bad it’s painful. I’m not sure what the savings was or what you were after but it’s pretty much a fail. Also you can easily find any cocktail recipe for any given ingredient online so I’m not sure why anyone would pay for these.

title: Awful graphics, hot mess
body: Down loaded and promptly deleted. The graphics are awful and hard on the eyes. It’s not intuitive. Drinks are very limited. No thank you,

title: Garbage
body: This app is no good. Contains very few liquor types. What app doesn't have hennessy? Fireball? Svedka?

title: Filtering is not helpful
body: Fun design but the searching for and filtering of recipes is not intuitive. Make saved filters and bookmarked recipes easier to find through one or two clicks.

title: Search function falls short
body: I search for “Gin Campari” and it returned Caipirinha.

title: Annoying
body: I’ve had this app for years. Every time they update, it loses my info so I have to start over with ingredients etc. Ridiculous. Also, the new monetization model is garbage. Why would anyone subscribe to this when countless stuff exists online and in the App Store. I paid for the recipe packs years ago, so I don’t mind paying- but if I had to subscribe I absolutely would have deleted.

title: Beware of Subscription
body: There’s so much to like about this app, the art style seems to be a bit divisive, but it’s really quite charming. Unfortunately almost all the recipes are locked behind a subscription. There’s not much value without it, and no option for a one-time purchase.

title: $1.99/month Subscription
body: I was about to buy the $11.99 full recipe unlock, but realized there were some recipe lists in the “coming soon” category. I decided to update my app to see if those recipe lists had been added, only to find that the in-app purchases for recipe lists had been replaced with subscriptions. I really like the app, but there’s no chance I’m going to spend $12/year or $2/month on a recipe list.

title: If I could.
body: If I could rate this out of 100 it’s a 69.69

title: Silly 8 bit interface ruins app with great potential
body: Disappointed that an app with so much potential would throw it all away with a gimmicky and ill-suited graphical interface approach that significantly degrades usability and function. Possible the regular UI is just as poor and not simply the fault of the cheap graphics, but I couldn’t even get far enough in basic utility with the app to test that out.

title: I want to love this app, but I hate it, but I still use it
body: The functionality is great, but please use modern graphics. The novelty of the 8-bit digital wears off in about 23 milliseconds. This app hurts my eyes. I love the functionality, but I hate looking at this app. The moment another app comes out that duplicates this functionality (as well as depth of recipe database), I will drop Mixel and move to something that doesn’t cause me to lose my vision. In the mean time, I’m begrudgingly using Mixel. Edit: Per the developer’s recommendation, I tried out Lush cocktails on the App Store. The recommendation was spot on as Lush is a much better executed app. It sounds like Mixel made a poor design choice early on and now they are stuck with it. Either way, I’m getting great cocktail recipes from Lush and it doesn’t hurt my eyes to look at!!

title: Not intuitive!!
body: I found this app to be very confusing.

title: It’s mid
body: Not the worst bar app but not the best. I’m underwhelmed by the only purchase options - either $2/month or pay the same (a laughable $0.01 savings) annually but NO lifetime option??? That would really make this a 5 star app! For the free version I only get access to maybe 200 basic recipes from lots of sources based on my personal well-stocked bar, so your results will vary. There are apparently “thousands” of locked recipes which require subscription. Based on very basic recipes I’ve seen so far it’s not very value added. This would be the best app if I could pay once now then opt in (to pay again or not) for future expansions. It’s just ok.

title: Latest Update Broke Features
body: With the latest update, when you are looking at cocktails in the ingredient tab and you go back, it takes you all the way back to the list of ingredients instead of to the list of cocktails you can make with that ingredient. Slightly inconvenient when looking at cocktails for an ingredient that’s used in 200+ recipes

title: Lost data
body: This was an excellent app, but now I’ve lost all my data, including recipes and bar stock. Really disappointing.

title: Great app terrible monetization
body: The only way to unlock all the recipes in this app is a subscription, either $2/month of $12/year.

title: Could have been great
body: I like the retro aesthetic of this app. It’s super functional and I like that it lets me track my ingredients as well as recipes. Unfortunately, I’m just not interested in a subscription. If I had the option of buying recipes in a one time purchase I might’ve stayed in. As it is there are two few free recipes and why would I pay a subscription fee when there are literally thousands of recipes available for free with a quick Google search.

title: Bad info
body: I wanted an app that can show me the other i friends to to drinks. I am inexperienced so i was hopping the “25 most used” non-alcoholic drinks would only have non alcoholic but half the list is alcohol

title: Subscriptions ruined this app
body: Mere months ago Mixel would have earned five stars. I bought the recipe packs because I support the authors' work and creativity. It wasn't working out for them apparently, because they've been replaced with a regular subscription. Jeez, I grumble about paying for both Netflix and Hulu—what makes them think I'm interested in dropping an enormous amount of money regularly for something I drink twice a week?

title: Cute at first, but frustrating to read on a phone.
body: Maybe the text is prettier on a tablet, but it’s just too small and funky to be enjoyable on iPhone SE screen. Functionality seems great. Wish I could apply a new font package.

title: Great Concept
body: This is a great concept. The graphics and fonts are a mess. Very hard to read. I’d suggest offering a non 8-bit option.

title: Doesn’t support landscape mode?
body: I downloaded it for my iPad thinking this could be a nice app for behind my bar, but it only comes up in letter and not landscape mode. Most people have a case for their iPad so that they can set it on a counter or something and read from. This seems like a fairly significant shortcoming in my opinion.

title: Great app with just two feature request
body: I love the app so much. It has tons of cocktails and allows me to see what I can make based on what I tell it I have and I love that I can write original recipes in app. However, unlike the cocktails that are featured in the app plus the extra when you pay for the app,’the original recipes don’t show the amount of dilution for the drink which is my only request for the app. The other request is to select the drinks you want to add to a cocktail menu.

title: Lifetime is so Expensive
body: Ok, I’ll begin by saying this app’s UI and its premium recipe list are fantastic. I love the style and the ingredient maximizer is a great feature. However, the lifetime subscription is pricey, especially since there are records of the lifetime price being far less than $50. It’s just so expensive…

title: Nice but…
body: Could be easier to navigate IMHO

title: Great, but i have a suggestion
body: I really like this app so far. But I noticed when i do a search of my recipes by ingredient the list no longer sorts by recipes i can make with my bar. Maybe I’m missing something.

title: Great, but no active improvement
body: Mixel is fantastic. It’s definitely the best app I’ve found for finding drinks, but it isn’t perfect. For example, you can’t hide a recipe, which seems pretty basic. The problem is, I don’t think that’s going to change, and that frustrates me when I am paying a subscription. This is a popular app, there’s a lot of folks sending their monthly fee to the devs. That it is essentially passive income for them is just a little frustrating. I dunno. Mixel is the best option for this type of app, but it is probably exactly as good as it will ever get.

title: Amazing
body: I love the art and creativity. I’m also very fond of the free options even though the paid options aren’t too expensive. I’d make it a 4.5/5 if I could. Things I’d like to see: - Options to add more backgrounds and glass types (even as paid add-on’s) - A one-time purchase option. I don’t like subscriptions, but I’d like all the good stuff if I could have it. - The ability to add specific brands of alcohol as ingredients (they could have a google plug to pull from public data.)

title: Best bar app out there… still, could improve a couple things
body: I’ve tried every bar app I could find. This is the best. I won’t go into all the things this app does well - that’s been covered by many others. Instead, I’m going to mention the one thing that kept this app from a 5-star for me. Entering ingredient portions is too restrictive. For instance, you add 1/3 oz of an ingredient (which is a very rare measurement for mixing drinks), but you can’t add 3/8 oz (which, although uncommon, is certainly more common than 1/3 oz). That’s strange. And you can’t add more than 99 units of any particular measurement. So, for instance, if you’re wanting to save a recipe that calls for 120 grams of something (which is what I’m trying to do right now), you can’t. I think this could be easy solved by allowing users to manually type in portions and units if desire. Leave the scroll bars for common measurements, but let me type in 120 grams or 1.5 cans (cans is not a unit option). Add that, and this is a 5-star app.

title: Awesome app for beginner bartenders.
body: Okay I love this apps asthetic and simplicity. I just wish I can get back to the “Bar” the middle tab.

title: Almost what I was looking for
body: This app is almost what I was looking for. It does a great job of keeping track of my bar inventory, however recipes are tedious to enter and if I don’t have an ingredient in my bar and it isn’t one of the preset items I can’t add it to the recipe without adding it to my inventory. Also when entering items into inventory there isn’t a category for garnishes or pantry items. These are the items that are not present and make it difficult to add recipes.

title: Good but.....
body: Why can’t I sort based off others reviews of a recipe? That just seems like a given if you’re going to ask for peoples reviews of cocktails. Need that feature added.

title: It’s really nice!
body: I am a huge fan of this app! I love the art style! I love that I can add my own recipes and then adjust them when I need to make larger amounts. It would be great if the iPad App had a landscape view since most of the time I’m using the iPad is when it’s connected to the keyboard.

title: Nice app. Sometimes sluggish
body: Nice app. Some times it is unusably slow especially when it is first opened after a few days of being closed. Lots of good recipes. I wish there was a way to rate the drinks you have made instead of just making them as tried.

title: Look forward to using it more and seeing more features
body: The thing that drew me in was he art style, being a huge old school gaming nerd. What kept me interested was the usefulness and potential of the app. I look forward to obtaining more packs in the near future, both to support the developers and obtain more recipes, and in time making this the primary way I look up drinks. I’m hopeful that with age this will be my primary resource for cocktail recipes. I do wonder if cocktails other users create or add will be available to the rest of the users. Fingers crossed!

title: Very good
body: Genuinely, this is such a dope app. I know people are probably looking to get all access styled cocktail apps for free. However for 15 dollars a year or a 50 dollar flat fee, this app is literally dirt cheap for the value it provides. Very intuitive so many useful features like the bar so you know what you can make with what you’ve got. Making your own cocktails is so intuitive and well made. Couldn’t recommend it enough for finding fun drinks to try and somewhere organized to store your own creations. You can even edit existing recipes to tailor them to your taste. Super cute app too.

title: Love the versatility
body: This app is great not only for its extensive repertoire but the easy ability to add your own concoctions to the library and to share them with friends via text that includes handy QR code for them to download it to their app

title: Cocktail bartenders easy choice
body: I’m a craft bartender and I reference this app and the drinks it lists all the time. Especially when I get thrown a weird request or rare request that I don’t know off the top of my head

title: Incredible
body: Finally, I have a way to store and rate my favorite cocktail recipes! This app has been a game changer for me. I have a place to document all the one-off cocktail recipes I find and love. The premium version has been 100% worth it to me—there is a very large variety of very good cocktail recipes loaded into the app and it’s introduced me to a lot of great recipes. And the cherry on top is the cute pixel style for your recipes and items in your bar. What more could a girl want?! :)

title: Excellent for home bars
body: This is one of the most comprehensive collections yet.

title: Indispensable
body: If you’re a cocktail aficionado, this app is indispensable.

title: Get this of you like flavors
body: Love it, I have had my cocktail awakening through this app, it was recommended to me by a friend and I have had a lot of great drinks from here. I would love for there to be a new tab or area in here for community recipes that you could add to your regular recipes tab from other users.

title: “No AI” option?
body: Have used & loved the app for years! Recently saw the addition of Bart. Can I disable or remove this? I don’t want any generative AI messing up your brilliant app. Thanks!

title: Fun to use, well-made
body: It’s a simple idea that was well-designed and well-built. I like the pixelated art style, I like building out my bar, and it’s fun to look up cocktails or add my own. My only request is a wider library of cocktails to search from, but at least it’s easy to add my own.

title: Best cocktail app around
body: Love this app, and I’ve tried a few. Happy to pay and access across devices. Would love API level and web access to my bars, and the recipe search could use some work, but it’s still great. Keep it up!

title: Professional and innovative!
body: Professional and innovative. It could be better with liquor/liqueur brands!

title: Simply the best
body: Truly my favorite app and has been for years. I’ve had it since it first came out! I believe I heard about it on Reddit directly from the developers when they were introducing it and looking for feedback. It’s clearly made by cocktail geeks and I LOVE that about it. The aesthetic is also perfection. Pixel font till I die!

title: Great app!
body: Easy to follow recipes with the right proportions. Flexible settings.

title: Fantastic App
body: This app is fantastic. First, it has all the drink recipes I could hope for … the standards, the exotic, the contemporary trends. Second, the app makes navigation a breeze; it’s easy to find drinks to make, or to find what bottles will have the biggest impact when added to my bar, or to find the drinks that I already love. Third, I love the social component, being able to rank drinks, see which drinks rank highly, and to get community feedback about recommended tweaks to a drink.

title: What a neat app!
body: From the aesthetic to the calculations, this app is a bundle of joy for the mixologist on the go or at home. The free version limits recipes, so I recommend buying the yearly subscription - it’s worth it!

title: Best
body: Best there is, I tried a lot of them.

title: Best drink app
body: Just a darn useful app. The price has never not felt like a bargain.

title: Excellent cocktail app
body: I am a highly proficient and sophisticated pandemic era home bartender and I purchased the unlimited lifetime version of this app. I have made over 200 different recipes, discovered countless new variations, been inspired to seek new ingredients, and learned a lot along the way. I own many cocktail books, and subscribe to several YouTube cocktail channels. This app continues to feel relevant and useful to me.

title: Essential cocktail app
body: I have been relying on this app for all cocktail making recipes since 2017. It’s great

title: Issues with Latest Update
body: This is the best cocktail app ever, and it’s not even close. However, the latest update (accidentally?) introduce a change that makes the app harder to navigate. If I want to view cocktails with, say, aquavit, and I select a cocktail from the list of cocktails, and then I click back, it takes me all the way back to the ingredient list instead of taking me back to the list of cocktails with aquavit. Same issue with recipe sources. If I want to see Smugglers Cove recipes, and I filter drinks for that source, and I click on a drink, and then click the back button, it doesn’t take me back to the list of SC recipes, but rather ALL my recipes. Please fix this!

title: Love it
body: For just a couple people making this app in their spare time, it’s honestly incredible. Fun and simple, yet has a very robust system that makes it easy to filter things in tons of ways. I appreciate the level of detail. Nice work!

title: Best bar app period
body: I almost never rate apps, but this one is just too good. I have downloaded several bar apps, but this is by far the very best. It goes way above all the others. Love the 8 bit bar with fridge. I wish I could give this app 10 stars

title: Excellent—the one you’ve been seeking
body: Categorizes spirits properly, has a great searchable system, history blurbs about each, ideas and markers to mark recipes you want to go back to or which are favorites, a rating system for the recipes/cocktails themselves. Really, this is the app you’ve been looking for.

title: Finally a free and easy to use app
body: All the other apps on the app store are nothing compared to this and this is free

title: This is it.
body: I’m not much an app reviewer. But when an app thinks things through and delivers the functionality I want…I gotta say something. Thanks for this app! So many things are helpful in how it’s setup. The Mixel Maximizer??? Exactly the information I want to know for my growing home bar. The sorting, grouping, searching, note taking, etc. I love it all. I’m admittedly no pro barista and don’t have the finest palate for cocktails…so I can’t speak to that stuff. But, this is my personal review. Well done app and I’ll gladly pay for the Premium.

title: Best Recipe App Bar None
body: I’ve tried many and this one is the absolute best. Easy to reference recipes on the fly. Create drinks and save to the platform, then share with you bar team. Batching drinks is super simple and very helpful. I appreciate the art style and over all simplicity of the app. Cannot recommend enough regardless of your skill level.

title: Perfect cocktail app!
body: The premium version of Mixel has literally everything I've been looking for in a cocktail app. Tons of recipes, ratings, the ability to bookmark and favorite recipes, as well as mark those that you’ve tried. You can make notes on recipes AND create your own. You can filter the list by a ton of different factors. AND you can sync all of it across devices. All that for a yearly subscription that doesn't break the bank. The only thing I can think to add is silly minor stuff like a more customizable color scheme or graphics that are slightly more recognizable. But honestly, It's great.

title: Best bar purchase for home bar
body: Big fan and constantly adding recipes to it

title: Well made
body: Very thought out and executed app

title: A home bartenders best friend
body: This app is the best resource for making drinks, and managing your bar’s inventory I could imagine. It is essential to me now.

title: Overall Excellent App
body: This app has been indispensable with my recent parties I’ve been hosting. As the bartender for my events, it’s allowed me to take my cocktail game to the next level. It was an easy choice to subscribe given the app’s value in this space. I am, however, very disappointed when it comes to content creation in this app. There are features here I’ve been trying to make use of to no avail. So far I have created a few ingredients that I didn’t find listed. Of those, almost all disappeared moments after saving them. Worse yet, creating a new cocktail this morning, I spent a good deal of time copying down all the pertinent info into the app, a detailed history, instructions, tasting notes, etc. Similarly to the mysteriously disappearing ingredients, my cocktail recipe, after saving and showing up for several minutes, mysteriously disappeared — never to be seen again. I would love to share more cocktails with the community and use them in the app for my own reference, but the time I take from my day to transfer these, only to see them disappear moments later, stops me in my tracks. I’m a busy man, and don’t have time to waste with flaky apps that don’t work. So while I will continue to use this as an excellent reference, the inability to depend upon it for adding missing content leaves me scratching my head as to where it fits into my workflow and rethinking that subscription. I had hoped it would be my one-stop-shop, but I think I’ll have to look elsewhere to record my menus and drink creations from other sources. Maybe these issues will be fixed in the future. Until then, 4 stars for a very useful reference. However, with content creation on the rocks, I can’t recommend it if your needs fall into that category.

title: Get this app
body: The most comprehensive and well organized cocktail app on the market. Thousands of recipes! Includes a Mixel calculator to identify which ingredient will allow you to create the most new recipes at your bar

title: THE go-to cocktail app
body: After trying several kinds of drinks apps I settled on this one because it lives up to its theme of simplicity while having so many diverse drinks. I bought four different “drink packs”back in 2019 when they sold them for $.99 - $2.99 but now I would say that the 12 bucks a year would still be worth it.

title: The Winner Bar none!
body: Absolutely love the app! It’s clean and has a great UI. I just want to leave a few suggestions that hopefully see life in future - Ability to choose a few cocktails and create cocktail menus for parties would be awesome! Bonus if there’s a way to generate a QR Code that opens a link. - Monthly cocktails added. There are so many places to pull from (YouTube, Instagram, PunchDrink, ImBibe) might be difficult though. - Add a section users navigate to that includes ALL user submitted cocktails so fellow users can sift through them and see what else is out there. - Cocktail competions where users submit their own drink and others can vote for winners. Be it monthly / Bi-monthly etc, could be fun and create more of a community.

title: Random idea
body: I love this app! The images are not as good as other cocktail apps, but I get the Mixel/Pixel association. It would be great if the random feature would only pick a random recipe based on what you already have on hand.

title: Best app ever!
body: Amazing for making drinks, creating new recipes, and using your ingredients!

title: Fantastic for discovering new recipes and building a home bar
body: The extensive catalog of cocktail recipes and system for telling you what you can make (either with the proper ingredients or close-enough substitutions) is wonderful for discovering new drinks, and the Mixel Maximizer function is incredible for telling you what to buy next to give you the most new possible recipes. This app has played a central role in my own exploration of cocktails and makes this hobby so much more approachable than it would otherwise be without it.

title: A nice surprise
body: I’ve tried probably dozens of drink recipe and/or ingredient-tracking apps—I installed about four different ones, including this one, on the same day. I seem to gravitate to this one. When i need a quick recipe, or can’t decide what to make, this is the one I tend to open. I got a new liquor about a week ago, and realized I should add it to my “bar”—I opened the app and found that I’d already added it sometime in the last week. That was when I realized I was no longer testing this app, I was using it regularly and relying on it. Forget brand names, forget “Order Now!” buttons, this app will tell you what you can make and how to make it with what you have on hand. Simple mission, simple art, simple interface, simply useful.

title: Bar tender and bar enthusiast’s companion
body: This app has been absolutely wonderful for home mixing, and we’ve enjoyed the huge variety of recipes in the paid version.

title: Super useful! So clever
body: Wish I found this sooner! They thought of everything - tags on flavor profiles of drink recipes, the ability to add to a shopping list. It’s so easy to add your current ingredients and the visual is also extremely helpful. Love!

title: Finally…
body: …someone got this right. Nothing more to say than buy it and use it. Oh, and please develop the same product for cooking!

title: Gotta Stock Them All
body: It’s an amazing app makes making cocktails a fun collection game triggers that gotta stock them all feel that finds you stopping by Liquor stores saying if I pick up a bottle of sweet vermouth I will unlock 35 more cocktails then I’ll pick up some oranges that’s like another 20 so far I’m at 330

title: GREAT app, but I’ve noticed something...odd
body: Ok, so, odd thing: Mountain Dew is in the ingredient list but there are no drinks that use it...and I’ve bought every add on lol

title: A complaint
body: 5 star game/app but I don’t know how much alcohol and sugar is in the ingredients also I can’t add alcohol volume

title: Really is good
body: I bought the whole package. Cheaper than a book. I list what I have in stock and easy to find recipes. I can bookmark what I want to make. Then review and mark what I have made and what I like. Super easy. Wide range of items. No issues. No glitches. Makes me happy.

title: Best cocktail app of many I have
body: Best cocktail app of many I have. I have over 10 different app, I paid much more for some of these apps, some of them are costly monthly or yearly membership but are so poor in content. This is my go to app. One of only three out there are worthy.

title: My favorite cocktail app
body: I have many sources for cocktails, and out of all them, this is my absolute favorite. It’s easy to use, I can filter through flavors, ingredients and even sources. It’s amazing. I also love how it doesn’t always get too specific with the ingredients and if it does, it gives me a replacement suggestion. Please keep adding recipes and new sources! Also some new color schemes for dark mode would be excellent. Thank you!

title: Excellent App for Budding Bartenders
body: This app has everything you need if you’re just getting into cocktails. It’s well designed, has tasty recipes, a good community of reviewers, and good sorting/search features. It’s totally worth the $12 for premium as well. Makes you feel like the ‘tender in Casino Royals, serving a classic Vesper to mysterious clientele.

title: Great App
body: Well thought out. It does exactly what you want it to do and then some. Thumbs up to the maker.

title: Everything you need!
body: This app has it all! You can add the ingredients that you always have and it suggests drinks for you to make, or it will calculate how many recipes you can make with buying just one more ingredient. Super intuitive and fun to use!

title: Indispensable
body: Love the 8-bit aesthetic and the intuitive usability, but most of all I love being able to search by ingredient. I can’t count the number of times I’ve had a few random bottles and Mixel has come to the rescue with quirky recipes to try out. You can add the contents of your liquor cabinet and it will prioritize recipes for which you already have the right ingredients. Like your very own Nintendo bartender. Highly recommended!

title: Best app out there but found a glitch
body: I love the app but I’ve noticed that when you share a drink with a friend that has a user created ingredient it doesn’t show up. Any idea how to fix this?

title: Literally my favorite app.
body: I’ve been spending too much money at the liquor store because of this. It’s super convenient, shows you what ingredients you have that are close enough to what you need for some drinks. Even shows you suggestions on what to get to expand you list of recipes. And it’s 8-bit, which looks really cool. It’s my favorite app I’ve ever downloaded. This might push me towards liver failure and that’s a risk I’m willing to take.

title: Best app for home mixology by far
body: If you like making drinks at home, this app is the best way to reference and record recipes. The Maximizer is extremely useful for people looking to grow their bar by recommending the bottle that will best expand their cocktail selection. I have an extensive book collection for cocktails, but Mixel is what I use when I'm actually making drinks.

title: Best cocktail app!
body: The best on the market! It has everything you need, at home or as a professional bartender.

title: So accessible, and such a cool style
body: Absolutely love this app. Super useful, great 8-bit style through and through. Paid for the annual membership after 20 minutes playing with it, and two weeks later it’s already paid for itself. Well done, developers!!

title: The best home bartending app ever
body: Ive been searching for a proper home bartending app for months, and I've finally found the best one. It looks cool, has great functionality, and many features that are unique to this app. The only downside is i spend more on alcohol now after using the mixel maximizer! One piece of feedback - there should be some way of searching for user created recipes across mixel’s database (definitely not on as a default in the search option, as otherwise you can end up with some not so great drinks); it would be cool to see what the community can come up with. Additionally, some users can get verified (so like professional bartenders, etc. and their custom recipes come with that verification note)

title: Legit
body: At first I couldn’t understand anything about this app but I kept coming back because I liked the idea. I’m glad I took the time to learn because this app is great for working bartenders or people with home bars. I can stock an imaginary bar with the same ingredients I have at the bar I work at. When a customer says “surprise me” I can check out this app for drinks that I could make with the ingredients at hand and tweak to make it my own. Recipes are from reputable sources in the industry.

title: So far so good, but a suggestion
body: I just downloaded this a few days ago, and so far I really like it. I saw some older reviews that said it was hard to use, but I definitely disagree. Very straightforward. Easy to enter things I have in my bar right now, and has a few staples already added. What I would really like to do is link to my friends and share recipes with them, and maybe the ability to make recipes public to share with a community. I need to try it out for a bit longer, but I am considering paying for the full version.

title: Great App!
body: There are a few apps out there some with more reviews. Ignore them, I’ve tried literally every one of them, yes even the one you are thinking of. This app is fantastic and allows you to see what drinks you can make with what you have in your cabinet and pantry. Also it’s free so downloading it should be a no brainer.

title: Great phone app needs better iPad support
body: I love the database of drinks. It’s easy to add things to your inventory so you can see what you can make on hand and can’t. Some people won’t like the pixel art, but I often see apps with ‘photos’ that aren’t accurate so it’s a mixed bag where ever you go. Great note taking and filtering. The things I’d change if anything would be to hand the dev an iPad Pro with a keyboard and beg for landscape mode. Adding custom ingredients is greats, would be nice (likely hard) to allow saying “this custom ingredient can sub for this generic or other inventory item”. All in alll it’s becoming my go to for storing recipes and keeping track of what I’ve tried.

title: Download this, then buy Premium.
body: The 8-bit format took a moment or two to get used to, but once I got the hang of it, HOLY COW. I plugged in every ingredient I had in my pantry and was off to the races. 5 minutes after making my first Negroni, I bought the Premium pack—as one reviewer mentioned, it was what one fancy cocktail would cost. Well worth it.

title: Best of the bar apps - and a suggestion
body: This app gets its right and also has a very extensive database of drinks (especially with the premium IAP) and ingredients and can categorize and sort the list well. The only thing I’m missing right now is a little more control on the randomizer. It would be great to be able to say “show me a random recipe with base spirit X and where I have at least 90% of the ingredients on hand”. Future version? (Well, and maybe a way to mark a recipe as “don’t show me this one again” or whatever the opposite of favorite should be...)

title: Absolutely Amazing
body: In the 10+ years I’ve owned an iPhone, I’ve never once written a review for an app. This is the first one, and it’s well worth it. For years since I’ve started making cocktails, it’s always been a good bit of effort to look up recipes or scour through my resources to figure out what I could make with the ingredients I have. This app is so amazingly intuitive that it has everything I need to organize my cocktail menu based on what I have. I can tell whoever made this app went through a great amount of trouble compiling all the recipes from the various resources out there. So I was very happy to pay the $12 to receive that very extensive library. I can’t sing the praises for this app enough! This app definitely deserves the most amount of recognition among the other apps in this category. Also, love the retro video game graphics. Nice touch 😃

title: Creative Quarantini!
body: We’re making a lot of cocktails and are tweeking recipes to our palate. Mixel is VERY helpful to keep us organized! Love it!

title: A really really well made app
body: I use this almost everyday. Exactly what you are looking for! Thanks Mixel!

title: Best cocktail app on iOS
body: My go to cocktail app. I often pick it up over my cocktail recipe books.

title: Future ideas...awesome app
body: I love this app. It’s awesome and really helps for parties. An idea would be to give you recipes based on what you already have after you add the bottles to your shelf. That would be great!

title: Paid and got nothing?
body: I paid for premium a while back. It shows so in the store, upon booting up the app I really only see the basic 80, if that. It offers to let me pay for premium or packs that should be available to install. :/

title: Cool App
body: I was just a wounded Boy who did not know how to mix drinks. Now I can thanks to this 8-bit Mario style hipster bar app.

title: Best cocktail app, bar none
body: This app is absolutely amazing for managing your bar and trying new recipes. I’d highly recommend paying for some of the premium recipes as they are great quality from highly renowned sources. I’ve tried a bunch of other cocktail apps and this one is hands down the best. Awesome devs who listen to the community. Highly recommend!

title: Wonderful!
body: I absolutely love this app! It’s everything I have ever wanting in a cocktail app. Every single detail from seeing what you can make with what you have, the shopping list, and my personal favorite the little bit that lets you see how much more you could make by adding whichever ingredients you’re thinking about. Also love how it tells you about subbing different things. Like in one recipe I saw it said I can use triple sec instead of having to buy cointreau. Also the flavor filters are amazing. Just all around a wonderfully done app and I definitely bought the entire unlock after fully exploring the initial options. Did not regret a thing.

title: Finally, a bar app that "thinks" like a bartender
body: The thing this app gets right is that spirit brand names fall onto categories of spirits, and some of those categories are similar enough to be somewhat interchangeable. Most cocktail recipes are developed as essentially advertising for specific brand names, which makes the recipes confusing for people who don't know much about them or which other spirits are likely to be similar enough in flavor profile to be used instead. This app does away with brand names for the base spirits altogether (though they're smart enough to include them in the database so you can still search for them) and tells you which of your character- driven liquers will work well enough when a recipe calls for something else. The only thing I actually need to use my experience-based bartending knowledge for when using the app is to make adjustments in recipe ratios to compensate for the flavor differences that I "know" to be true for such substitutions, but I can see future iterations of this app (or one like it) being able to do this as well if the flavor characteristics are appropriately coded in the back end. Great job you guys, this is the app I recommend to people who are looking to get going with their home bar.

title: Fun and useful
body: I found this app when my bartender at The Haymaker in Raleigh NC created a custom drink with Pimms for me called “A Sworthy Brit” and texted me a Mixel screenshot of the recipe. Wish we could see recipes from other users so I could see it in the app, but I get the “curated” thing. Anyway it’s a handy app. Love the design, and I easily input my home bar, unlocked everything in the app, and now have hundreds of great drink recipes. Well done!

title: Incredible!!
body: Absolutely love this app. Extremely helpful for a new bartender as well as someone experienced looking for their next creation! I love the maximizer function as it allows me to know which ingredient i need to buy next in order to maximize the amount of cocktails i can make! 5 Stars!

title: Cool & Creative.
body: Very inventive, I don’t need the other apps I downloaded to test out - this will do fine. This app gives you all the freedom in the world to stock, learn, create and explore. It’s digital theme, sound effects and the ability to customize not only your digital bar but the little things like the font style, sound, and even the apps color options add a great touch - the little things add up. A great amount info and overall style, I love how we can build a collection of our own creations. I really don’t drink much, but it’s very interesting to try new drinks and experiment here and there ...wether we’re good at that or not. Doesn't stop me from taste testing. The app makes it more fun. And lastly this app was free but I see myself visiting their Mixel Shop soon to see what other ingredients are out there.

title: Finally
body: I’ve tried every cocktail app from Lush to Highball to Old Sport. Mixel is clearly a cocktail lovers app by folks who clearly care about cocktails. Since this is a PG channel I’ll avoid the positive expletives, and pare back to a simple air-five 🙏🏻 When you unlock the content, you’re going to have a good time. Sure, some folks are going to make a fuss about the 8-bit graphics “not being for them,” but guess what? It’s cute. Great product photography is expensive for independent developers and (more importantly) completely unnecessary in this context. You have the recipe; just mix it (you’re clearly in need of a cocktail). Sure, for legibility, I’d opt for a single space font like Monaco, but that’s truly my only niggle. Smart shelf. Smart ingredients. Smart shopping list. It’s a no brainer. Well done to all involved.

title: Really good
body: I loved this app not only for the graphics but also for the lots of recipes, I’ve done only 3 of them but I’m practicing to improve my bartender skills, loved it!!!

title: Love this app
body: Love this app. Love the graphics. Only thing I would work on is the filter screen. I would like to filter by ingredient instead of pack. I guess I know why you didn’t add it, because there are hundreds of ingredients. And liquor isn’t separated. Hmm tricky. Only annoying because I was looking for gin drinks and Tom Collins isn’t in the gin pack. Maybe add an option to hide partial ingredient recipes based on level. The filter screen is a little confusing. But otherwise I love the app and can’t wait for more packs! Mixel Maximizer is really clever.

title: The best app
body: This app is great! We have been using it to make all sorts of cocktails at home, and have learned so much about what we can do with fun and new ingredients!!

title: Fantastic Mixing App
body: With amazing art and great feature set is immediately became my go to cocktail curating app. With the developer actively working within r/cocktail community it makes for a much more receptive experience. Birdman thanks for listening to all of our feedback and I’m so excited for the new features and drink packs that are coming. You already got me hooked on the premium within 5 minutes of opening the app!

title: Wonderful Home Bar App
body: It is wonderful to have an app on hand that allows me to experiment with the various ingredients I already have. Thank you Mixel Cocktails!

title: Well Designed, Fun, and Helpful!
body: Whether you only need to consult the app for an eggnog recipe once a year at the holidays, or you need an everyday companion, this app is perfect. What if I told you that there was a way to tell you phone what is in your Bar and refrigerator, and it would store that information and show you drinks you can make currently, as well as drinks you might be able to make with a few more ingredients? Until Mixel, there wasn’t an elegant solution. Mixel takes old school art and mixes it with helpful information to take you from a regular guy or gal to a top notch at-home (or full-time) bartender.

title: WOW!!!
body: Such a great app! Always struggled to figure out drinks that I could make with my closet of random drinks but with the app I don’t have to worry about it. Also, the drinks that are in the shops seem totally worth it! Best cocktail app by far!
